title: evidence-cli run check and answer check

targets.text: evidence-cli reads a finished associate run from its export: it re-checks every fact against the saved results, counts them, writes reviewer flags beside the run, and, as a separately named result, says whether the run's answer matches recorded expected values; associate imports it for its own re-check
both commands exist and associate's suite passes importing them
associate, which imports the re-check as a library and calls the answer check from its measurement runner; an operator or reviewer checking one export or many from the command line
associate's test suite passes using only names this spec lists as public
evidence-cli is the template scaffold with no domain code; the only re-check of an associate run lives inside associate, and nothing anywhere marks a run's answer right or wrong
git ls-files evidence at origin/main lists only scaffold modules

evidence check reads one export or many and prints counts per run and summed, each disagreement with the harness's own counts, and reviewer flags, and writes the flags to a file beside the run without touching the run's files; evidence grade takes an answer text and a task's expected values and returns matches, does not match or cannot tell, citing the rule that decided; the same code is importable, and associate uses it in place of its own
both commands run on the committed fixture exports and their output is identical on a second run
one place holds the check, so associate gets leaner and every consumer gets the same fixes; and it gives the planned comparison a grader that is not the harness under test
associate's groundwork spec names evidence-cli as its grader and re-check

100% of the shared matcher and hand-back vectors pass in evidence-cli; counts over the fixture exports equal a hand count; a second run prints a byte-identical report; every file in the export is byte-identical after both commands; and for every fixture task the recorded answer is graded as matching and a hand-written wrong answer as not matching
each of the five checks is a named test in the evidence-cli suite

the matcher, the checker, the counts, the export loader and the run-result summary move from associate/accuracy into evidence-cli with their tests, keeping function names and results; the public names are listed in the documentation and a change to any of them is a breaking release
every function associate imports today exists under the documented name and returns the same result on the saved test exports

the checker's settings (source kinds, the reason-to-check mapping, the minimum quote length) are an explicit input; the command accepts a settings file and otherwise uses a bundled default that it names in its output
running evidence check with no settings file prints which default settings it used and their version

evidence check reports, per run and summed, the counts by kind and by source kind, and lists each place its own re-check disagrees with the counts the harness wrote; a run with no facts is reported as not applicable, not as zero
on a fixture whose report.json was edited to a wrong count, the command names that count as a disagreement
reviewer flags are written to a file beside the run, in a location the run did not write, and no file of the export is modified or created inside it
a checksum of every file under the export directory is unchanged after the command

evidence grade takes the answer text as an explicit input, with the task's expected values, and returns matches, does not match or cannot tell, with the expected items found and missing; it never reads the facts list to decide, and calls no model
the result is unchanged when the export's facts.json is absent, and a grade is reproduced exactly on a second run

expected values are data with a schema and a version: items that must appear, items that must not, and alternatives, compared after the same normalisation the matcher uses; a result names the schema version it was graded under
two results are reported as comparable only when their schema versions are equal, and a task file with an unknown key is refused

the words printed keep the two results apart: the run check is described as counts of checked quotes and backed conclusions, the answer check as a match against recorded expected values, and neither as quality, correctness of the work, or accuracy; each output carries the line that a complete trail does not mean the work is correct
a test fails if either command's output contains the words quality score or accuracy
the shared test vectors ship inside the evidence-cli package, so associate can compare its own copy with the installed one
associate's copy and the packaged copy are compared by a test in associate and are equal at the pinned versions
CLAUDE.md is re-initialised from its seed into a real project file that states the two results, the public library names and the no-dependency rule
the file no longer contains the seed's re-init instruction
no runtime dependency, no model call and no network access; the same inputs give the same output
the package's dependencies list is empty and no module imports a network library
evidence-cli never imports associate, and never edits a run; the TypeScript checker stays in associate's extension
no file under evidence/ imports associate, and the fixture checksums are unchanged by the test suite
this work does not build the general trail of the build brief (request, spec, plan, code, validations), its rubric or a final score, and does not settle the overlap with storybook-cli
no command added here prints a final score
the run check states which export formats it supports; an export with a newer format than it knows is reported as unsupported with the version it found, never checked with older rules
a fixture whose format marker says a version above the supported one produces an unsupported result and no counts

an expected item that is a number or an identifier matches only as a whole token, so 9 does not match 19 and 0.5 does not match 10.5; free-text items match after whitespace is collapsed, with case kept or folded as the item says
for each fixture task, an answer holding a longer number that contains the expected one is graded as not matching
cannot tell is returned only for stated causes (an empty answer text, or expected values that name no item), each named in the result; an answer that simply lacks an expected item is does not match
an empty answer gives cannot tell with its cause, and an answer missing one required item gives does not match

when the flags file cannot be written the command says so and exits with an error code, and an option sends the file to a named directory or suppresses writing; the printed report is the same either way
run on a read-only location, the command exits non-zero with a remediation line and still prints the counts

acceptance_criteria: every matcher case in evidence/data/matcher_vectors.json passes against evidence.accuracy.matcher.check_quote
evidence.accuracy.counts.fact_counts and the per-source-kind counts return the same values as the associate versions on the ported tests
the vectors are readable from the installed package through one documented function, and a test reads them that way
the packaged vector file is byte-identical to associate/contract/matcher_vectors.json at commit 266dad3
tasks.instruction: Copy matcher.py and counts.py from the associate repository at commit 266dad3 (github.com/agentculture/associate), directory associate/accuracy/ and its tests into evidence/accuracy/ (new package, with __init__.py), changing only import paths and docstring references. Copy associate/contract/matcher_vectors.json to evidence/data/matcher_vectors.json and add a small function that returns its parsed content from the installed package (importlib.resources). Port tests/test_accuracy_matcher.py to tests/test_matcher.py and the count tests from tests/test_accuracy_check.py to tests/test_counts.py. Write the tests first and see them fail before the code exists. Files owned: evidence/accuracy/__init__.py, matcher.py, counts.py, evidence/data/, tests/test_matcher.py, tests/test_counts.py. Do not touch evidence/cli/.

tasks.summary: Move the hand-back checker, the export loader and the run summary; make settings an explicit input; report unsupported export formats
acceptance_criteria: every hand-back case in the shared vectors passes against evidence.accuracy.check.check_handback
each of the eight public functions is importable from its evidence.accuracy module and the ported tests pass unchanged in what they assert
the default settings loader returns the bundled settings and a version, and check_handback gives the same result with them as with the associate file at 266dad3
an export whose format version is above the supported one returns an unsupported result naming the version found, with no counts; an export with no marker is still reported as not applicable
no module under evidence/ imports associate, and the test run leaves every file under tests/fixtures/ unchanged (checked by checksum in a test)
tasks.instruction: Copy check.py from the associate repository at commit 266dad3 (github.com/agentculture/associate), directory associate/accuracy/ and its tests into evidence/accuracy/check.py, keeping every public function name (parse_source_ref, check_handback, load_export, load_handback_input, inspect_export, accuracy_result) and its results. Port tests/test_accuracy_check.py (checker parts), tests/test_accuracy_replays.py and tests/test_accuracy_runs.py with tests/fixtures/accuracy/. The checker already takes its settings as an argument: add evidence/data/accuracy_defaults.json (a copy of associate/contract/accuracy.json at 266dad3 with its version) and a loader that returns it and its version. New behaviour: a constant names the supported walk format versions; an export whose format marker is above the highest supported one yields a result marked unsupported with the version found, and no counts. Write the tests for the new behaviour first and see them fail. Never import associate. Files owned: evidence/accuracy/check.py, evidence/data/accuracy_defaults.json, tests/test_check.py, tests/test_replays.py, tests/test_runs.py, tests/fixtures/. Do not touch evidence/cli/.

tasks.summary: Build the run check command module: one export or many, sums, disagreements, flags file
acceptance_criteria: on the fixture exports the per-run counts and the sums equal a hand count written in the test
a fixture whose report.json states a wrong count is listed as a disagreement with both values, and a run with no facts is reported as not applicable and adds nothing to the sums
the flags file is written beside the export directory and a checksum of every file under the export directory is unchanged
with an unwritable location the report is printed, the message says the flags file was not written, and the exit code is the environment error code; --flags-dir and --no-flags exit 0
with no --settings the output names the bundled default settings and their version; with --settings it names the file
two runs on the same inputs print byte-identical output, in text and in --json
tasks.instruction: Write evidence/cli/_commands/check.py exposing register(sub) and the handler, following the pattern of the existing command modules (results through _output, failures as CliError, --json). It takes one or more export directories, an optional --settings file, --continue-from, --flags-dir and --no-flags. For each run: counts by kind and by source kind from evidence.accuracy; a list of disagreements between the re-check and the counts in the run's own report.json (both values shown); not applicable for a run with no facts; unsupported for a newer format. Then the sums over applicable runs. Reviewer flags go to a file beside the run: the directory that holds the export directory, in evidence/flags.json, never inside the export directory. If that cannot be written, print the report, say the file was not written, and exit with the environment error code; --flags-dir writes elsewhere and --no-flags skips writing, both exiting 0. The output states which settings were used (file or bundled default with version). Do not register the verb in evidence/cli/__init__.py, the explain catalog or learn: another task does that. Test by calling the handler with an argparse namespace. Tests first. Files owned: evidence/cli/_commands/check.py, tests/test_check_command.py.

tasks.summary: Build the answer check library and its expected-values schema
acceptance_criteria: an answer holding every required item and no forbidden item is matches; one missing a required item, or holding a forbidden one, is does_not_match, with the items named
a number or identifier item does not match inside a longer number or identifier, and does match as a whole token next to punctuation
an empty answer or expected values naming no item gives cannot_tell with its cause, and nothing else does
a task file with an unknown key or without schema_version is refused with a reason, and every result names the schema version
grading the same inputs twice returns equal results, and the module imports nothing outside the standard library and evidence
tasks.instruction: Write evidence/answer/ (new package): a schema for a task's expected values as data with a schema_version, holding items that must appear, items that must not appear, and groups of alternatives where one must appear; each item has a text and a kind (number, identifier or text) and, for text, whether case is folded. A function grade(answer_text, expected) returns matches, does_not_match or cannot_tell with the items found, the items missing, the forbidden items present, the schema version and, for cannot_tell, its cause. Matching: text items after the whitespace collapsing used by evidence.accuracy.matcher.normalise; number and identifier items only as whole tokens, so 9 does not match 19 and 0.5 does not match 10.5. cannot_tell only for an empty answer text or expected values that name no item. A task file with an unknown key or no schema_version is refused with the reason. The function never reads an export and calls no model. Tests first. Files owned: evidence/answer/, evidence/data/expected_values.schema.json, tests/test_answer.py.

tasks.summary: Build the answer check command module
acceptance_criteria: for each fixture task the recorded answer is reported as matches and a hand-written wrong answer as does not match
the answer can be given as a file or on standard input, and the result is identical
a refused expected-values file exits with the user error code and a remediation line
two runs on the same inputs print byte-identical output, in text and in --json
tasks.instruction: Write evidence/cli/_commands/grade.py exposing register(sub) and the handler, following the existing command modules. It takes --answer-file (or - for standard input) and --expected (a task's expected-values file), with --json. It prints the result of evidence.answer.grade: matches, does not match or cannot tell, the items found and missing, and the schema version. It takes no export directory and reads no facts file. Exit code 0 for any of the three results; a user error for an unreadable or refused input. Do not register the verb in evidence/cli/__init__.py, the explain catalog or learn. Tests first, calling the handler with an argparse namespace. Files owned: evidence/cli/_commands/grade.py, tests/test_grade_command.py.

tasks.summary: Register both commands, document them in explain and learn, and fix the wording that keeps the two results apart
acceptance_criteria: evidence check and evidence grade run from the console entry point, and evidence explain check and evidence explain grade describe them
uv run teken cli doctor . --strict passes
a test fails if either command's output contains quality score or accuracy, or lacks the line that a complete trail does not mean the work is correct
the existing CLI tests still pass
tasks.instruction: Register check and grade in evidence/cli/__init__.py, add their entries to evidence/explain/catalog.py and to both forms of evidence/cli/_commands/learn.py, as the repository's rule for adding a verb requires; run the rubric gate (uv run teken cli doctor . --strict) and make it pass. Fix the printed wording in both command modules: the run check is described as counts of checked quotes and backed conclusions, the answer check as a match against recorded expected values; each output carries the line that a complete trail does not mean the work is correct; neither uses the words quality score or accuracy. Add tests/test_wording.py asserting this on the text and --json output of both commands. Files owned: evidence/cli/__init__.py, evidence/explain/catalog.py, evidence/cli/_commands/learn.py, tests/test_wording.py, and wording-only edits to the two command modules.

tasks.summary: End-to-end and boundary tests on the fixture exports
acceptance_criteria: five separately named end-to-end tests exist, one for each part of the success signal, and pass
a test fails if pyproject.toml gains a runtime dependency or a module under evidence/ imports associate, a network library or subprocess
a test fails if any command's output contains the words final score
tasks.instruction: Add tests/test_end_to_end.py and tests/test_boundaries.py. End to end, through the console entry point: every shared vector passes; counts over the fixture exports equal a hand count; a second run prints a byte-identical report; every export file is byte-identical after both commands; each fixture task's recorded answer is graded as matching and a wrong one as not matching. Name the five tests so each can be cited alone. Boundaries: the built package metadata has an empty dependency list; no module under evidence/ imports associate, a network library (socket, urllib, http, ssl) or subprocess; no command prints a final score. Tests only: if a test exposes a defect, report it instead of changing code outside tests/. Files owned: tests/test_end_to_end.py, tests/test_boundaries.py.

tasks.summary: Rewrite CLAUDE.md from its seed, document the public library names, and release notes for 0.7.0
acceptance_criteria: CLAUDE.md no longer contains the seed's re-init instruction and states the two results, the public names and the no-dependency rule
every name listed in docs/library.md is importable, checked by a test, and the list includes the eight functions associate imports
the version is 0.7.0, the CHANGELOG has its entry, and markdownlint passes on the changed files
README.md names both commands and says that a complete trail does not mean the work is correct
tasks.instruction: Replace the seed CLAUDE.md with a real project file: what evidence-cli does today (the run check and the answer check, and that they are separate results), the public library names associate imports and the rule that changing one is a breaking release, the no-dependency rule, how to run tests and the rubric gate, and what is not built (the build brief's general trail, rubric and final score; the storybook-cli overlap is not settled). Add docs/library.md listing each public name with its module, and a test that imports every name listed there. Update README.md with the two commands and a link to associate's groundwork spec as the first consumer. Bump the version to 0.7.0 with the repository's version-bump script and write the CHANGELOG entry, which states that before this release the package was the template scaffold. Files owned: CLAUDE.md, README.md, docs/library.md, CHANGELOG.md, pyproject.toml (version only), tests/test_public_names.py.

risks.text: evidence-cli must be released to PyPI before associate can merge the change that imports it; a defect found after release needs a second release
how associate's TestPyPI pre-release job resolves a first-party dependency has not been examined
the rubric gate (teken cli doctor --strict) may impose requirements on the two new verbs that this plan has not listed
the moved Python tests were written after the code and never seen to fail; tests shown to fail when a rule is removed are not part of this plan
symlinks inside an export that point outside it were not examined
